papers.title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
papers.abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. Results: The results showed that heat-inactivated PC-01 significantly decreased the Disease Activity Index and H&E histopathological scores (p < 0.05). It also reduced the serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokin
papers.summary: In a DSS-induced mouse model of colitis, heat-inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 reduced disease activity and histopathological damage and lowered serum pro-inflammatory cytokines. The protective effect appears to be mediated through modulation of the gut microbiota and improvement of intestinal barrier function.

papers.title: Probiotics as a Barrier Against Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli in Contaminated Rice-Protein-Based Infant Formulas.
papers.abstract: Background/Aims: The presence of pathogens such as Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli in infant formulas, even at concentrations below the detection threshold, poses a health risk. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to limit pathogen proliferation. This study evaluated two probiotic strains (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 and Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis IM-1) to inhibit the growth of these pathogens under simulated conditions. Methods: Assays were conducted using reconstituted infant formula supplemented or not with the probiotics combination and challenged with E
papers.summary: This study tested whether two probiotic strains (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 and Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis IM-1) can inhibit Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli growth in reconstituted rice-protein-based infant formula. The probiotics were assessed under simulated conditions to see if they act as a protective barrier against pathogen proliferation in contaminated formula. The work evaluates a potential food-safety intervention for infant formula.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of developmental-category-associated fungal communities in the gut contents of Achatina fulica, an intermediate host of Angiostrongylus cantonensis.
papers.abstract: The invasive giant African snail (Achatina fulica) poses serious agricultural and ecological threats and serves as an important intermediate host of the zoonotic parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, which causes human eosinophilic meningitis. While its gut bacterial microbiome has been extensively characterized, the gut mycobiome remains largely uncharacterized. In particular, variations in gut fungal communities across developmental stages remain unknown, limiting our understanding of the A. fulica gut holobiont.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the fungal communities (mycobiome) in the gut contents of the giant African snail Achatina fulica, an invasive species and intermediate host for the parasite that causes eosinophilic meningitis. It compares fungal community composition across different developmental stages of the snail, filling a gap since the gut bacterial microbiome was already well studied but the mycobiome was not. The work provides a baseline description of how gut fungal communities vary with snail development.

papers.title: From Prediction to Mechanism: Explainable AI for Plant-Microbiome Multi-Omics Integration and Biological Discovery.
papers.abstract: Predicting complex phenotypes from plant-microbiome multi-omics data has advanced significantly with machine learning and deep learning. However, traditional black-box models remain limited by their focus on predictive performance rather than mechanistic biological understanding. To bridge this gap, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a key framework to transform biological data analysis from correlation mapping to hypothesis-driven discovery. This review synthesizes current advances in XAI methodologies, including post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically
papers.summary: This review synthesizes explainable AI (XAI) approaches for integrating plant-microbiome multi-omics data, arguing that black-box predictive models must be complemented by interpretability methods to move from correlation to mechanistic insight. It surveys post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically interpretable models, framing XAI as a bridge between prediction and hypothesis-driven biological discovery.

papers.title: Bacterial community profiles of soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve, Philippines.
papers.abstract: The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve harbors diverse microorganisms with potential biotechnological applications, yet bacterial taxonomic profiling across its watersheds remains limited. Amplicon metagenome sequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene revealed Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as dominant phyla, with Actinobacteriota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexi, Myxococcota, Methylomirabilota, Bacteroidota, Nitrospirota, and Planctomycetota present at varying abundances.
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing to profile bacterial communities in soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve in the Philippines. Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota were the dominant phyla, with several other phyla present at varying abundances across watersheds. The work provides a baseline taxonomic survey of soil bacteria in this understudied tropical forest reserve.

papers.title: Functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover across coral-associated microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coral-associated microbiomes are fundamental to holobiont health and resilience, yet their community structures often demonstrate high taxonomic variability across host species. Whether such variability results in functional instability or reflects pervasive metabolic redundancy remains unclear. Here, we investigated microbial taxonomic structure, functional potential, and community assembly mechanisms across 15 coral species using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. These communities exhibited extreme taxonomic heterogeneity, high beta-diversity, and the absence of a universall
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA sequencing and shotgun metagenomics across 15 coral species to show that coral-associated microbiomes vary enormously in taxonomic composition but remain functionally similar, indicating widespread metabolic redundancy. The findings suggest that different microbial taxa can perform the same ecological roles, helping explain how coral holobionts maintain function despite high taxonomic turnover.

papers.title: Exploratory associations of gut microbiota composition with HBeAg and HBsAg status in nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B.
papers.abstract: HBeAg and HBsAg reflect viral replication and host immune status and are important determinants of treatment responsiveness in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The gut microbiota, a key component of the gut-liver axis, may influence immune regulation and antiviral outcomes. This study characterized gut microbiota profiles across different HBeAg and HBsAg statuses in CHB patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. Fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 29 healthy controls (HC) and 101 NA-treated CHB patients without cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, including 30 HBeAg-po
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 101 nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B patients and 29 healthy controls to explore whether gut microbiota composition differs by HBeAg and HBsAg status. The work characterizes microbiota profiles across serological groups, suggesting potential links between the gut-liver axis and viral/immune markers, though the exploratory design and modest sample size limit causal inference.

papers.title: Exploring antimicrobial resistance in wild and domestic animal populations: combining publicly available data with BV-BRC resources to introduce bioinformatics in an undergraduate classroom.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatics blends the fields of biology, statistics, computer science, and information technology for the processing and analysis of genomic data. Despite the growing demand for trained bioinformaticians and a positive job market outlook, most undergraduate institutions struggle to integrate bioinformatics into their life science curricula. Educators face numerous barriers to incorporating bioinformatics into their classes, including technical issues and expertise. To address this need, we are developing web-accessible, course-based materials for general microbiology, infectious disease, g
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of web-accessible, course-based bioinformatics materials for undergraduate microbiology and infectious disease classes, using publicly available data and BV-BRC resources to explore antimicrobial resistance in wild and domestic animal populations. The work aims to lower barriers to integrating bioinformatics into life science curricula by addressing technical and expertise challenges faced by educators.

papers.title: Recovering anaerobic bacterial genomes in saliva, tumour and blood whole genome sequencing data from patients with prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Microbial constituents in the gastrointestinal tract, the urine and prostate tissue are being linked with clinical differences in prostate cancer, and a recent meta-analysis has linked periodontal disease to this cancer. Several hypotheses exist regarding how specific bacteria can contribute towards the development of prostate cancer. Recovering microbial genomes, and their genomic features, from clinical samples and investigating fine-scale taxonomy is a critical first step in investigating causality. Here, we describe the microbial diversity of samples associated with prostate cancer. Metage
papers.summary: This study recovered and characterized anaerobic bacterial genomes from saliva, tumour, and blood whole-genome sequencing data of prostate cancer patients, revealing microbial diversity associated with the disease. It provides a fine-scale taxonomic and genomic resource that could help investigate whether specific bacteria contribute to prostate cancer development, building on links between periodontal disease and this cancer.

papers.title: Integrating complementary datasets for constructing microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways.
papers.abstract: Microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways play a central role in host health, but studying them is limited by the data available. Large clinical microbiome cohorts often lack metabolomic measurements, while multi-omics studies with paired profiles are typically small or incompletely phenotyped. Combining such complementary datasets is challenging: the metabolite is not measured in the clinical cohort, microbiome data are high-dimensional and compositional, and log-ratio analyses depend on an arbitrarily chosen reference taxon.
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of linking microbiome and metabolome data to disease by integrating large clinical microbiome cohorts (which lack metabolomics) with smaller multi-omics studies (which have paired profiles but limited phenotyping). The authors propose a method that handles high-dimensional compositional microbiome data and the arbitrary reference-taxon problem in log-ratio analyses to construct microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways. This enables pathway discovery that neither dataset type could support alone.

papers.title: Protocol for mixed methods study exploring the gut-brain health among South Indian population.
papers.summary: This paper presents a protocol for a mixed-methods study investigating the gut-brain axis in a South Indian population, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches. The study aims to explore how gut health relates to brain health in this understudied group. As a protocol, it outlines the planned methodology rather than reporting results.

papers.title: A gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking.
papers.summary: This study integrates gut microbiota, metabolite, and host gene data to construct a composite score that stratifies rheumatoid arthritis patients into subtypes and predicts their response to treatment. The authors validate key microbial-metabolite-host gene relationships using in silico knockout simulations, supporting the score's mechanistic plausibility. The work offers a multi-omics biomarker framework for RA, though clinical validation in independent cohorts remains to be established.

papers.title: An optimized flow cytometry sorting-sequencing workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction bias in sorted microbial communities.
papers.abstract: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) followed by metataxonomics is commonly used to probe the composition of microbial subpopulations with a functionality of interest. Metataxonomic analysis of sorted low-microbial-biomass samples is prone to contamination and bias introduced during sorting and DNA extraction. To improve metataxonomic accuracy, the DNA yield obtained by the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit was first maximized. FACS-sequencing using the optimized DNA extraction method distorted the composition of sorted microbiota by introducing sheath fluid contaminants, termed the FACSome. Sinc
papers.summary: This study optimizes a FACS-to-sequencing workflow for low-biomass sorted microbial communities, first maximizing DNA yield from the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit and then identifying a 'FACSome'—sheath fluid contaminants that distort sorted microbiota composition. The optimized workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction biases, improving metataxonomic accuracy for sorted subpopulations.

papers.title: DNAharvester: A Nextflow Pipeline for Analysing Highly Degraded DNA from Ancient and Historical Specimens.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences.
papers.summary: DNAharvester is a Nextflow pipeline designed to process highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens, addressing challenges like short fragments, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and contamination. It aims to reduce spurious mapping and reference bias, improving the reliability of downstream population genetic analyses for aDNA studies.

papers.title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA.
papers.abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. Notably, microbial community str
papers.summary: Using sedimentary ancient DNA and stable isotopes from a Lake Daihai sediment core, the authors reconstructed centennial-scale changes in lake microbial community structure and function. They found that deterministic assembly processes dominated historically, but stochasticity increased markedly after 1850, coinciding with the end of the Little Ice Age and intensifying human impacts. This shows that climatic and anthropogenic forcings differentially shape microbial community assembly over long timescales.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, sleep and coronary artery disease: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Inadequate and poor-quality sleep is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Gut microbiota may play a role in sleep regulation. However, the associations between gut microbiota, sleep, and CAD risk, and the causal nature of these associations, remain unclear. We performed a 2-step Mendelian randomization analysis using summary-level data to assess the association between gut microbiota and CAD and the potential mediating roles of sleep-related traits (i.e., chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short sleep, and long sleep) herein. The inverse-variance weigh
papers.summary: This study used two-step Mendelian randomization with summary-level genetic data to test whether gut microbiota influence coronary artery disease risk and whether sleep traits mediate this relationship. The analysis examined multiple sleep-related traits (chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short and long sleep) as potential mediators between gut microbiota and CAD. The abstract is truncated before results are reported, so the specific causal estimates and mediation proportions are not available.

papers.title: Causal relationship between oral microbiome, circulating inflammatory proteins and lung cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Recent research showed that oral microbiomes (OMs), as the main source of lung microbiomes, were associated with lung cancer (LC), but the causal relationship and mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the immune mechanisms of LC through the "OM - inflammatory proteins - LC" axis. Instrumental variables covering 43 oral microbial taxa, 91 circulating inflammatory proteins, and LC subtypes were obtained from large-scale genome-wide association study summary data of European origin. We employed Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to validate causal links between the OM and LC a
papers.summary: Using Mendelian randomization on large European GWAS summary data, the authors tested causal links between 43 oral microbial taxa, 91 circulating inflammatory proteins, and lung cancer subtypes. They propose an 'oral microbiome–inflammatory proteins–lung cancer' axis, identifying specific taxa and inflammatory mediators that may causally influence lung cancer risk. The work is exploratory and relies on genetic instruments, so findings are hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

papers.title: Development of a novel diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia based on microbial community characteristics.
papers.abstract: The lung microbiota plays a key role in pneumonia. A correct diagnosis in the early stage helps treatment and limits severity progression of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This study develops a diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) by analyzing the microbial community characteristics of the lung microbiota. The approach aims to enable early and accurate diagnosis, which is critical for timely treatment and reducing disease severity.

papers.title: Transmission of lactic acid bacteria: a case study of the human vaginal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are among the microorganisms to which humans are most frequently exposed, largely via consumption of fermented foods and probiotics and through interpersonal contact. Such continued exposure to LAB does not necessarily result in stable engraftment, raising fundamental questions about which factors mediate successful LAB transmission and niche specialization across human-associated microbiomes. Here, we rethink transmission of LAB across the human life course, spanning food-associated, within-host, and interindividual routes, highlighting that LAB transfer can occur a
papers.summary: This review reconsiders how lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are transmitted between humans and across body sites, using the vaginal microbiome as a case study. It argues that frequent exposure to LAB through food, probiotics, and interpersonal contact does not guarantee stable colonization, and highlights the need to understand which factors drive successful transmission and niche specialization. The authors map transmission routes across the human life course, including food-associated, within-host, and interindividual pathways.

papers.title: MIMEco: multi-objective metabolic modeling to predict and explain pairwise interactions.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models provide a mechanistic framework for quantitatively exploring an organism's physiology and its interactions with the environment. However, their use in microbial community modeling has been limited since it usually relies on community-wide objective functions or the integration of community abundance data. Nevertheless, predicting microbial interactions is crucial for understanding ecosystem dynamics and thus requires dedicated methods. Here, we introduce Metabolic Interaction Modeling in Ecosystems (MIMEco), an open-source Python package that predicts pairwise mic
papers.summary: MIMEco is an open-source Python package that uses multi-objective metabolic modeling to predict and explain pairwise microbial interactions without relying on community-wide objective functions or abundance data. It provides a dedicated framework for mechanistic prediction of interactions from genome-scale metabolic models, addressing a key limitation in microbial community modeling.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals gut segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring linked to host phenotypic maturation in Taihu geese.
papers.abstract: Taihu geese are valued for efficient utilization of fibrous feed resources and for desirable meat quality, yet how gut microbial organization varies across intestinal regions and physiological stages, and how these changes relate to host phenotype, remains unclear. We integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ITS sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and host phenotyping to characterize intestinal microbial ecology in Taihu geese at 160 days of age (D160; physiological stability stage) and 450 days of age (D450; late-laying stage). Spatial profiling of the D160 group across the duodenum, jejunum, ileum
papers.summary: This study integrated 16S rRNA, ITS, and shotgun metagenomic sequencing with host phenotyping to characterize how gut microbial communities vary across intestinal segments and between two physiological stages (160 vs. 450 days) in Taihu geese. The authors identify segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring that correlates with host phenotypic maturation, highlighting links between gut ecology and host physiology in this breed.

papers.title: Oral Actinomyces Species Exposure is Associated with Anxiety-Like Behavior, Mitochondrial Remodeling, and Altered GABAergic Pathways.
papers.abstract: The human oral microbiome is increasingly recognized as a contributor to brain health, yet its mechanisms remain unclear. We previously found an enrichment of oral Actinomyces species in chronic cannabis smokers.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether oral exposure to Actinomyces species, previously found enriched in chronic cannabis smokers, can influence brain function and behavior. The authors report that such exposure is associated with anxiety-like behavior in an animal model, alongside mitochondrial remodeling and changes in GABAergic signaling pathways. The work suggests a potential mechanistic link between specific oral bacteria and anxiety-related neurobiological changes.

papers.title: mums2: an R package for database-dependent and -independent analysis of untargeted metabolomics data.
papers.abstract: mums2 is an open-source R package that enables users to analyze data from untargeted metabolomics analyses. mums2 provides features that parallel existing tools for analyzing 16S rRNA gene sequence data, including data curation, annotation, clustering of features into operational metabolomic units (OMUs), and analyses based on ecological metrics.
papers.summary: mums2 is an open-source R package for analyzing untargeted metabolomics data, offering both database-dependent and database-independent workflows. It mirrors common 16S rRNA amplicon analysis tools, providing data curation, feature annotation, clustering of features into operational metabolomic units (OMUs), and ecological metric-based analyses. This gives microbiologists and metabolomics researchers a familiar framework for processing and interpreting untargeted metabolomics data.

papers.title: Fast and accurate taxonomic domain assignment of short metagenomic reads using BBERT.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomes from complex environments such as soil uncover vast biodiversity. Yet most short reads produced by shotgun sequencing cannot be taxonomically or functionally annotated, as they lack a sufficiently comprehensive reference, obscuring the true structure and function of microbial communities. We introduce BBERT, a nucleotide large language model optimized for short reads. Testing on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, we found that BBERT identifies bacterial sequence syntax without relying on reference databases, enabling accurate assignment of taxonomic domain, coding potentia
papers.summary: BBERT is a nucleotide large language model trained to classify short metagenomic reads by taxonomic domain without relying on reference databases. Tested on soil metagenomes, it accurately assigns domain-level taxonomy and coding potential to reads that would otherwise remain unannotated, addressing a major gap in complex-environment metagenomics.

papers.title: Optimized approaches to profile low biomass DNA and RNA virome in the upper respiratory tract of beef cattle.
papers.abstract: Viruses play a key role in cattle respiratory tract (RT) health, yet, profiling the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome (DNA and RNA viruses) from deep nasopharyngeal swabs (DNS) remains challenging due to their low biomass, lack of well-defined enrichment approaches, and a high proportion of unclassified viral sequences. This study aimed to optimize DNS preservation, nucleic acid extraction, and bioinformatics pipelines to enhance URT virome characterization in beef calves.
papers.summary: This study optimized methods for preserving deep nasopharyngeal swabs, extracting nucleic acids, and analyzing bioinformatics pipelines to better characterize the low-biomass DNA and RNA virome in the upper respiratory tract of beef calves. The optimized workflow improves detection of viruses from challenging samples with high proportions of unclassified sequences, supporting respiratory health monitoring in cattle.

papers.title: Integrated In Silico Analysis Reveals ABC Transporter ATP-Binding Protein as a Therapeutic Target in Helicobacter pylori.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori remains a major cause of gastric diseases, while increasing antimicrobial resistance highlights the need for novel therapeutic targets. Here, we developed a comprehensive computational target-prioritization framework integrating Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify pathogen-specific drug targets in H. pylori J99. Twelve conserved domain families comprising 746 proteins were identified, and domain abundance showed a weak negative correlation with versatility
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline combining Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to prioritize drug targets in Helicobacter pylori J99. The authors identify ABC transporter ATP-binding proteins as pathogen-specific therapeutic candidates, addressing the need for new targets given rising antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction.
papers.abstract: It is common to build predictive models for complex phenotypes, such as diseases, where sample sizes are often limited by the cost of data collection. Machine learning and statistical methods are widely used in these cases. However, they may fail to identify high-quality features and lead to suboptimal models with high underfitting or overfitting risks. Here, we present mBoost to identify low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction. Importantly, it provides confidence on model performance, helping researchers avoid the frustrating cycle of model switching for pos
papers.summary: The authors introduce mBoost, a tool that identifies low-quality features and suboptimal models in phenotype prediction tasks, which is especially useful when sample sizes are limited. It provides confidence estimates for model performance, helping researchers avoid repeatedly switching models without clear justification. This aims to improve the reliability of predictive modeling for complex diseases and other phenotypes.

papers.title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal s
papers.summary: This study performed functional metagenomic analysis on fecal samples from a prior randomized controlled trial of fungal nutraceutical (Micodigest®) supplementation in colorectal cancer surgery patients. It found that the supplement modified the functional potential of the gut microbiome, moving beyond taxonomic shifts to show changes in microbial gene content and pathways. These functional changes may help explain the previously observed favorable inflammatory effects in these patients.

papers.title: Reduced-Complexity Cultivation of Human Oral Anaerobic Bacteria Using a Microdroplet-Based Culturomics Platform.
papers.abstract: The human oral microbiota contains fastidious anaerobes that remain uncultivated due to resource competition and overgrowth by dominant species in conventional plating. Culturomics approaches leveraging droplet-based microfluidics offer an alternative by physically compartmentalizing microbial cells. We established a polydimethylsiloxane-based microdroplet platform to isolate anaerobic bacteria from human oral rinse samples. Droplet generation conditions were optimized using fluorescent beads, and bacterial loading at the collection-drop level was evaluated using Escherichia coli. Two downstre
papers.summary: The authors developed a microdroplet-based culturomics platform using polydimethylsiloxane devices to isolate fastidious anaerobic bacteria from human oral rinse samples. By physically compartmentalizing cells in droplets, they aim to overcome resource competition and overgrowth that limit conventional plating. The abstract describes optimization of droplet generation and bacterial loading but does not report specific new isolates or findings.

papers.title: Early-Life Gut Microbiota and the Pediatric Gut-Lung Axis: A Systematic Review of Clinical, Preclinical, and Mechanistic Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The early-life gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in immune maturation and may influence respiratory health through the gut-lung axis. However, evidence linking microbial development, dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions to pediatric respiratory outcomes remains heterogeneous. This systematic review aimed to synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence on the pediatric gut-lung axis and its underlying mechanisms. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD4202510
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on how the early-life gut microbiota influences pediatric respiratory health via the gut-lung axis. It examines links between microbial development, dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions, finding the evidence heterogeneous but supportive of a role for gut microbes in immune maturation and respiratory outcomes.

papers.title: Metagenomic Bioprospecting of Bioremediation-Related Genes in Amazonian Aquatic Ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Environmental monitoring of contaminated freshwater systems still lacks curated genomic resources tailored to bioremediation-oriented screening. In this study, we developed a curated catalogue of 546 genes from 80 microbial species associated with heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, detoxification and related functions and applied it to river metagenomes from four municipalities in Pará, Brazilian Amazon: Altamira, Bragança, Marabá and Paragominas. Functional annotation was performed using eggNOG-mapper and metagenomic reads were aligned against the curated catalogue with Bowtie2.
papers.summary: The authors built a curated catalogue of 546 bioremediation-related genes from 80 microbial species and used it to screen river metagenomes from four municipalities in the Brazilian Amazon. By annotating with eggNOG-mapper and aligning reads with Bowtie2, they demonstrate a targeted approach for detecting heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, and detoxification genes in environmental samples. The work provides a reusable genomic resource for bioremediation-oriented monitoring of contaminated freshwater systems.

papers.title: Use of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing to Investigate Respiratory Pathogens in Influenza-Negative Nasopharyngeal Swabs From Cameroon's National Influenza Surveillance.
papers.abstract: In Cameroon, national influenza surveillance identifies influenza-positive cases, but the causes of non-influenza ARIs remain poorly characterized. We applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate respiratory pathogens in influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected through national influenza surveillance.
papers.summary: This study applies metagenomic next-generation sequencing to influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected through Cameroon's national influenza surveillance system, aiming to characterize the non-influenza respiratory pathogens causing acute respiratory infections. It demonstrates the utility of mNGS for pathogen discovery and surveillance in resource-limited settings where conventional diagnostics leave many ARI cases unexplained.

papers.title: Goat and cow milk merits distinct nutritional and functional properties based on simulated gastrointestinal digestion of infant.
papers.abstract: The nutritional and functional properties of goat and cow milk in digestive tract of infant is unclear. Applying simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion method, this study aims to systematically compare digestibility, peptide profiling, and immunomodulatory role of goat and cow milk, and further characterize their role in regulating homeostasis of gut microbiota and metabolism. It's found that the degree of hydrolysis and number of detected peptides was higher in goat milk (GM), while the relative abundance of predicted allergic peptides was higher in cow milk (CM). In addition, the expres
papers.summary: Using a simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion model, the study compared goat and cow milk and found that goat milk was digested more extensively, producing more peptides, while cow milk contained a higher relative abundance of predicted allergenic peptides. The two milks also differed in their effects on gut microbiota and metabolic homeostasis, suggesting distinct nutritional and functional properties for infant nutrition.

papers.title: A high-resolution spatial model of the primate gut microbiome defines niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of the gastrointestinal microbiome is shaped by strong physicochemical gradients along the gut, yet many region-associated microbial niches remain poorly resolved in humans. Here, we used the rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) as a spatially resolved primate model to profile 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and targeted bile acid metabolomics, complemented by comparative human datasets. Microbial communities exhibited strong spatial stratification along the gastrointestinal tract, while host
papers.summary: This study maps the primate gut microbiome at high spatial resolution by profiling 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract of rhesus macaques using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and bile acid metabolomics. The authors show that microbial communities are strongly stratified along the gut and identify niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism, with comparisons to human datasets. The work provides a spatially resolved primate model for understanding region-specific microbial niches that remain poorly resolved in humans.

papers.title: WasteFams: a database of protein families from global wastewater microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein fa
papers.summary: WasteFams is a new database that catalogs protein families found in wastewater microbiomes from around the world, built by integrating hundreds of metagenomes, metatranscriptomes, and reference genomes. It provides the first systematic, protein-level characterization of functional diversity in wastewater microbial communities, offering a resource for researchers studying wastewater surveillance and environmental microbiology.

papers.title: Biases in high throughput sequencing methods affect microbial molecular ecology networks and keystone taxa identification in the Cinnamomum migao rhizosphere and phyllosphere.
papers.abstract: The rhizosphere and phyllosphere microbial symbiotic interactions are crucial factors affecting plant health and productivity. How to authentically reflect the species interactions and assembly processes that shape shaping microbial communities has attracted extensive attention from ecologists. The construction of most microbial networks relies on amplicon sequencing data, neglecting both total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions. The impacts of sequencing resolution ratio, microbial domain, and quantification methods on microbial interspecies interactions and network parameters st
papers.summary: This study examines how biases inherent in high-throughput sequencing methods—such as sequencing resolution and quantification approaches—distort the construction of microbial co-occurrence networks and the identification of keystone taxa in the rhizosphere and phyllosphere of Cinnamomum migao. By comparing network parameters across different sequencing resolutions and domains, the authors show that methodological choices can substantially alter inferred species interactions and keystone taxa assignments. The work highlights the need for caution when interpreting amplicon-based ecological networks and suggests that incorporating total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions improves the authenticity of network reconstructions.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups.
papers.summary: This study compared the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients using metagenomic sequencing, aiming to identify microbial differences associated with resistance status. It addresses a gap in direct comparisons between these patient groups and may reveal microbiome features linked to TB pathogenesis or treatment outcomes.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of the early gut microbiota development in Nipponia nippon.
papers.abstract: The crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) is an endangered bird whose early gut microbiota development remains poorly understood. To address this gap, this study integrated metagenomics and metabolomics to investigate the dynamic succession of gut microbiota and metabolism in naturally hatched chicks during early development.
papers.summary: This study integrates metagenomic and metabolomic profiling to characterize how the gut microbiota and its metabolic output change during early development in naturally hatched crested ibis chicks, an endangered species. It provides one of the first longitudinal descriptions of microbial succession and associated metabolite shifts in this bird, offering baseline data that could inform conservation and captive-rearing strategies.

papers.title: Metagenomic and culture-dependent characterization of between-field variation in phosphorus-cycling microbial communities and functional potential across tobacco-safflower rotation fields.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms contribute to soil phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P acquisition, but P-cycling microbial communities and functional associations across tobacco-safflower rotation fields remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study combines metagenomic sequencing with culture-based isolation to characterize phosphorus-cycling microbial communities in the rhizosphere across tobacco-safflower rotation fields, focusing on between-field variation in community composition and functional potential. The work provides a survey of which P-transforming taxa and genes are present and how they differ among fields, linking community structure to phosphorus-cycling functional capacity.

papers.title: Pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented transcriptional response of the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT to acidic pH.
papers.abstract: Acidic environments impose energetic constraints on ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), although some acid-tolerant lineages remain capable of ammonia oxidation at low pH. The transcriptional responses of acid-tolerant AOB to low-pH conditions remain poorly resolved. Here, we characterized the pathway-level response of Nitrosospira sp. NT by integrating a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome with comparative metatranscriptomic data from cultures incubated for 24 h at pH 5.0 or pH 8.0. Transcript abundance was not uniformly reduced among the metabolic pathways examined at pH 5.0. Genes assoc
papers.summary: This study examined how an acid-tolerant ammonia-oxidizing bacterium, Nitrosospira sp. NT, responds transcriptionally to low pH (5.0 vs 8.0) over 24 hours. Using a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome combined with metatranscriptomics, the authors found that transcript levels were not uniformly reduced across metabolic pathways at acidic pH, suggesting a maintenance-oriented rather than broadly suppressed transcriptional response.

papers.title: Bacterial metagenome in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without OSCC by next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oral dysbiosis has been associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC); however, most microbiome studies rely on 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing, limiting species-level taxonomic resolution.
papers.summary: This study uses next-generation metagenomic sequencing to profile bacterial communities in dental plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), moving beyond the species-level limitations of 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The work provides a higher-resolution characterization of oral dysbiosis associated with OSCC across multiple sample types.

papers.title: Baseline co-occurrence of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii is associated with greater increases in selected short-chain fatty acid-related pathways following resistant starch type 2 intervention across diverse populations.
papers.abstract: Type 2 resistant starch (RS2) can be fermented by the gut microbiota and contribute to short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production; however, microbial responses to resistant starch vary substantially across individuals and populations, and the role of baseline microbiota in this variability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated four publicly available paired metagenomic datasets representing diverse experimental and host contexts and performed cross-dataset analyses of taxonomic and functional responses. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii was among the taxa consistently enriched
papers.summary: By integrating four public paired metagenomic datasets, the authors show that individuals whose baseline gut microbiota already contains both Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii respond to type 2 resistant starch with larger increases in short-chain fatty acid-related pathways. This baseline co-occurrence pattern holds across diverse populations and experimental contexts, suggesting it could help predict who benefits most from resistant starch interventions.

papers.title: Genomic insights into bacterial communities of coenocytic algae using metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.abstract: Coenocytic algae are organisms that undergo karyokinesis without cytokinesis, resulting in multinucleated cells. Most research on bacterial communities in coenocytic algae has used 16S rRNA sequencing, primarily focusing on the order Bryopsidales of green coenocytic algae. Recent studies have analyzed metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from algal hosts across multiple taxa, such as Chlorophyta, Phaeophyta, and Rhodophyta, revealing further insights into bacterial biosynthetic machinery and potential symbiotic relationships. Given the cosmopolitan distribution of coenocytic algae, such as Bryo
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to characterize bacterial communities associated with coenocytic algae, which are multinucleated organisms formed by karyokinesis without cytokinesis. Prior work relied mainly on 16S rRNA sequencing of Bryopsidales green algae, but this analysis extends across Chlorophyta, Phaeophyta, and Rhodophyta hosts, revealing bacterial biosynthetic machinery and potential symbiotic relationships. The work provides genomic-level insight into host-associated microbiomes in a broadly distributed but understudied algal group.

papers.title: TSLC: differential abundance analysis method for identifying biologically relevant known microbes.
papers.abstract: Identifying biologically relevant microbes is a crucial task in human microbiome studies. Numerous computational and statistical methods have been proposed for this task. However, most existing methods are based solely on taxonomic information, even when whole-metagenome sequencing data are available, and thus cannot account for the fact that different microbes can perform the same or similar functions (known as functional redundancy) and for the contribution of unknown microbes to functional abundance. Hence, the identified differentially abundant microbes might not be biologically relevant t
papers.summary: The paper introduces TSLC, a differential abundance analysis method for microbiome studies that incorporates functional information from whole-metagenome sequencing rather than relying solely on taxonomic profiles. By accounting for functional redundancy and the contribution of unknown microbes, TSLC aims to identify microbes that are more biologically relevant to the phenotype under study. This addresses a key limitation of existing taxonomic-only approaches.

papers.title: Effects of cultivation of herbaceous perennials on soil microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impacts of cultivating different herbaceous perennials on the rhizosphere microenvironment, nitrogen-cycling microbial communities, and functional genes in black soils of urban green spaces in Northeast China, thereby providing a scientific basis for rational urban plant configuration and interspecific differences in soil nutrient cycling. Focusing on five commonly utilized herbaceous perennials in Changchun (Lycopus lucidus [P-LL], Salvia japonica [P-SJ], Hemerocallis fulva [P-HF], Hosta ensata [P-HE], and Pseudolysimachion spicatum [P-PS]), this study integr
papers.summary: The study compares how five herbaceous perennial species grown in urban green spaces in Northeast China affect rhizosphere soil microbial communities and nitrogen-cycling functional genes. It finds that plant species identity shapes microbial community structure and nitrogen-cycling potential in black soils, supporting species-specific plant selection for urban landscaping and nutrient management.

papers.title: Metagenomic profiling reveals that divergent fire-adaptive strategies drive distinct fungal succession in pine litter decomposition.
papers.abstract: Decomposing litter is a critical driver of fuel bed formation and forest fire regimes, yet how divergent plant fire-adaptive strategies influence litter chemistry and subsequent fungal decomposition dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 6-month reciprocal litterbag experiment by incubating litter from two contrasting pine species-the fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis and the fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola-in both their own native habitat and that of the other species, coupled with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession and lignocellulolytic functional profiles
papers.summary: This study used a reciprocal litterbag experiment with two pine species that have contrasting fire-adaptive strategies (fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis and fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola) combined with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession during litter decomposition. The authors found that divergent fire-adaptive strategies drive distinct litter chemistry and fungal community trajectories, with corresponding differences in lignocellulolytic functional profiles. The work links plant fire adaptation to belowground decomposer dynamics, with implications for fuel bed formation and forest fire regimes.

papers.title: Beyond community state types: vaginal microbial diversity and CST-IV signatures are associated with pregnancy in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.abstract: Despite significant progress in assisted reproductive technology, in vitro fertilization (IVF) pregnancy rates remain suboptimal. Although the vaginal microbiome has been implicated in IVF outcomes, prior studies often overlooked embryonic aneuploidy, a major confounder. This study aimed to investigate the association between the vaginal microbiome and pregnancy outcomes in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.summary: This study examined whether vaginal microbiome composition is linked to pregnancy success in IVF cycles using only euploid (chromosomally normal) embryos, removing a major confounder from prior work. It found that both overall vaginal microbial diversity and specific signatures of community state type IV (CST-IV) were associated with pregnancy outcomes. The results suggest the vaginal microbiome may influence implantation even when embryo chromosomal status is controlled.

papers.title: Effects of trait stacking on the maize phyllosphere microbiome: a shotgun metagenomic comparison.
papers.abstract: Current safety assessments for stacked-trait transgenic crops underrepresent the phyllosphere, a critical interface directly exposed to transgenic products, warranting strengthened risk evaluation. Here, we employed metagenomics to characterize the phyllosphere of three maize lines under herbicide-free conditions: wild-type (Corn.CK), herbicide-resistant single-trait (transgene of cp4-epsps, Corn.S), and insect- and herbicide-resistant stacked-trait (transgene of cry1Ab and cp4-epsps, Corn.D). Shannon diversity showed a consistent trend toward higher values in the cp4-epsps single-trait line t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the phyllosphere microbiome of three maize lines: wild-type, a single-trait herbicide-resistant line (cp4-epsps), and a stacked-trait line (cry1Ab + cp4-epsps), all grown without herbicide. Shannon diversity trended higher in the single-trait line, suggesting that trait stacking may alter the leaf-surface microbial community, though the abstract is truncated and full conclusions are unclear. The work argues that phyllosphere communities should be included in safety assessments of stacked-trait transgenic crops.

papers.title: Probiotics in type 1 diabetes: immunomodulatory mechanisms and the unresolved question of clinical efficacy.
papers.abstract: Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is a common autoimmune disease worldwide, which is associated with imbalanced gut microbiota. Intestinal dysbiosis plays a key role in the pathogenesis of T1D, and it may affect immune tolerance and autoimmune responses of pancreatic islet β-cells. As a potential immunomodulator, probiotics can help restore this balance, regulate immune responses, and reduce the risk of T1D. Although probiotics offer a logical immunomodulatory strategy to restore microbial and immune homeostasis, the translational gap between robust preclinical mechanisms and inconsistent clinical outcome
papers.summary: This review examines how gut dysbiosis contributes to type 1 diabetes pathogenesis and how probiotics might restore microbial and immune balance to protect pancreatic β-cells. It highlights that while preclinical studies show strong immunomodulatory mechanisms, clinical trial results remain inconsistent, leaving the translational potential of probiotics for T1D unresolved.

papers.title: Marked variation in the bacterial microbiota of commercially produced Greek kefir products revealed by full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
papers.abstract: Kefir is a fermented dairy beverage characterized by a complex microbial community that contributes to its technological and sensory properties and has been associated in previous studies with potential health-related effects. While the microbiota of kefir grains has been extensively studied, information regarding the bacterial communities of commercially produced Greek kefir remains limited. The aim of the present study was to characterize the bacterial community composition of commercially produced kefir products collected from different regions of Greece using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequ
papers.summary: This study used full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize the bacterial communities in commercially produced Greek kefir products from different regions. The authors found marked variation in microbiota composition among products, highlighting inconsistency in commercial kefir production. This provides a baseline characterization of Greek kefir microbiota that may inform quality control and future health-related studies.

papers.title: Integrating Mendelian randomization with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to investigate gut microbiota-associated genetic signals and molecular characteristics in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) represents one of the most prevalent malignancies among men globally. Accumulating evidence implicates gut microbiota dysbiosis in the initiation and progression of prostate cancer; however, the causal relationship and underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. This study integrated Mendelian randomization (MR), bioinformatics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics to systematically investigate the genetic associations between gut microbiota and prostate cancer risk and characterize the expression patterns of microbiota-associated c
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study combines Mendelian randomization with single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to probe whether gut microbiota composition causally influences prostate cancer risk and to map the expression patterns of microbiota-associated genes in tumor tissue. The integrative approach links genetic instruments for microbial taxa to prostate cancer outcomes and then characterizes candidate genes at cellular and spatial resolution within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Cervico-vaginal microbiota and antimicrobial resistance patterns in relation to different reproductive statuses in cattle: a field study from Nepal.
papers.abstract: Vaginal bacterial communities are increasingly recognized as key determinants of fertility in cattle. This study explored bacterial communities in the cervico-vaginal mucus of healthy heifers, cows with cervicitis, repeat-breeding, and cows within the 35-day postpartum period using the microbiological culture method (n=35) and sequencing of the V3-V4 hypervariable regions of 16S rRNA gene (n=18), along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Micrococcus spp. and Enterobacter spp. were the top two bacteria isolated across the groups. Alarmingly, antimicrobial sensitivity tests revealed a hig
papers.summary: This field study from Nepal characterized cervico-vaginal bacterial communities in cattle across different reproductive statuses (healthy heifers, cervicitis, repeat-breeding, and postpartum cows) using culture and 16S rRNA sequencing, finding Micrococcus and Enterobacter as the dominant genera. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed alarmingly high resistance among isolates, highlighting a potential link between reproductive tract microbiota and antimicrobial resistance in livestock.

papers.title: Oliceridine and morphine differentially modulate the gut microbiota-intestinal barrier axis in a rat postoperative pain model.
papers.abstract: Oliceridine is a novel G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist with potentially improved gastrointestinal tolerability compared with conventional opioids. However, its impact on postoperative intestinal homeostasis-specifically the gut microbiota and intestinal barrier-remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study compares oliceridine, a G protein-biased mu-opioid agonist, with morphine for their effects on gut microbiota and intestinal barrier integrity in a rat postoperative pain model. The authors report that the two opioids differentially modulate the microbiota-intestinal barrier axis, suggesting oliceridine may have a distinct gastrointestinal profile. The work is preliminary and animal-based, but points to a possible tolerability advantage worth clinical follow-up.

papers.title: Dynamic changes in gut microbiota of three breeds of stud boars pre- and post-amoxicillin administration.
papers.abstract: Amoxicillin is a commonly used broad-spectrum antibiotic in pig farming, valued for its cost-effectiveness and efficacy in addressing prevalent swine ailments. However, the specific effects on the gut microbiota of stud boars and the trajectory of microbial recovery post-antibiotic withdrawal remain insufficiently elucidated.
papers.summary: This study tracked gut microbiota changes in three breeds of stud boars before and after amoxicillin administration, examining how the microbial community is disrupted and how it recovers after the antibiotic is withdrawn. It provides breed-specific insight into antibiotic-induced dysbiosis in an understudied livestock population.

papers.title: Prebiotic dietary fibers, gut microbiota, and short-chain fatty acid production: from fermentation mechanisms to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: The importance of the gut microbiota in regulating host homeostasis, immune responses, metabolism, and dietary interactions is increasingly recognized. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), microbial metabolites produced through the fermentation of dietary substrates, play a central role in mediating these interactions. Drawing on mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and insights from in vitro host-microbe fermentation models, this review critically examines how prebiotic dietary fibers have influenced the human gut microbial ecosystem, fermentation pathways, and SCFA production over the past
papers.summary: This review examines how prebiotic dietary fibers shape the gut microbial ecosystem and drive short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production through fermentation. It synthesizes mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and in vitro host-microbe fermentation models, and discusses pathways toward clinical translation of these findings.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform designed to support knowledge-driven microbiome research by combining microbial data with metabolomic and literature-based associations. The platform aims to address fragmentation in existing databases and knowledge graphs, which tend to focus narrowly on genomic information. It offers a unified environment for intelligent microbial applications, though the abstract does not detail specific methods or validation results.

papers.title: Potential involvement of a TLR4-associated CD155/TIGIT pathway in Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced immunosuppressive microenvironment formation in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis may promote an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in oral squamous cell carcinoma through a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling axis. The authors propose that bacterial stimulation of TLR4 drives ERK-dependent upregulation of CD155, which engages the inhibitory receptor TIGIT on immune cells to suppress antitumor immunity. This links oral microbiome dysbiosis to immune evasion in OSCC.

papers.title: Modulation of microbiota by traditional Chinese medicine in chronic inflammatory airway disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of animal studies.
papers.abstract: A growing number of studies have indicated that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can regulate microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway disease (CIAD). Nevertheless, no systematic review or integrated analysis has summarized relevant evidence to date, limiting the clinical application of TCM in this field.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes animal studies on how traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) modulates the microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway diseases. It is the first integrated analysis of this evidence, aiming to support the clinical application of TCM in this field.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tongue-image analysis may provide an objective, low-cost, and non-invasive adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines whether artificial intelligence applied to tongue images can serve as a non-invasive screening tool for gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders. It frames AI tongue-image analysis as a potential low-cost adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification, addressing the invasiveness and accessibility limits of upper GI endoscopy. As a review, it synthesizes existing evidence rather than presenting new primary data.
